triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: Same as index 0: the §122 surcharge was zeroed on entry_is_line_a/entry_is_line_b (China-301-list and aluminum exemplar flags) rather than on the source's exclusion-list and §232-covered exemptions, and the Brazil/forced-labor components applied by origin alone with no line-list membership test.
triage.triage_notes: Same pattern as index 0; changed-formula signature identical apart from the redundant-parenthesis count. Chapter-prefixed new parameter is ch03_s232_steel_heading_rate.
triage.verifier_justification: The change is a genuine fidelity correction — the §122 surcharge version in force 2026-02-24 to 2026-07-23 is re-gated, and the PR states the old coupling "unlawfully suppressed the surcharge on §301-member lines for all origins" — so "not_a_defect"/"mechanical" are refuted. But the kind is mis-labeled: entity (CustomsEntry), period, origin tests and output surface are identical pre and post; what was wrong is that the §122 exemption branch was keyed to predicates carrying a different provision's meaning. The same module defines `entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a` and `entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_b` (post lines 1907/1924, unchanged), while §122's own proof atoms cite entirely different exceptions (the "exclusion list under heading 9903.03.03" and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper ... provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04"), and entry_is_line_a simultaneously gated `list_1_additional_ad_valorem_rate` for China-301. That is a branch grounded on the wrong provision, which the fix re-grounds — the untraceable_branch definition — rather than a wrong entity, population or scope.

Evidence trail: diff /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-maxghenis-TheAxiomFoundation-axiom-encode--claude-worktrees-zealous-heyrovsky-31a96b/86103d8f-b97f-4559-a96c-7e79bdbe616d/scratchpad/diffs/us/a9562cfd44/002.diff; pre/post windows saved at .../scratchpad/pre_ch03.yaml and post_ch03.yaml.

Why untraceable_branch over wrong_entity_or_scope: the decisive defect is flag conflation, not mis-targeting. Pre-fix, one caller input carried three unrelated statutory meanings — entry_is_line_a was the reciprocal-annex exclusion flag (9903.01.32), the China-301 list-1 gate, and a §122 exemption trigger; entry_is_line_b was the reciprocal-metals flag (9903.01.33, aluminum only), the China-301 2024-action gate, the §232-aluminum gate and the second §122 exemption trigger. Outside the five witness exemplar lines no consistent assignment exists, so the generated chapter-wide module encoded a §122 exemption the cited provision does not state. Note also that pre-fix §122 keyed the metals exemption to an aluminum-only flag while its atom cites aluminum, steel and copper — a secondary under-representation of the same exception.

The commit bundles three different things; only the first is the defect the classification rests on:
1. Re-grounding of §122, §232-aluminum, §201 and the four China-301 slots onto membership-semantic inputs (the defect; untraceable_branch).
2. Brazil/forced-labor: pre-fix `if entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b: 0 elif origin_is_brazil: ...` becomes `if entry_is_brazil_301_listed and origin_is_brazil: ...`. This removes an ungrounded suppression but converts an exclusion-structured rule into an inclusion-list rule, and the module's own summary says these inputs "currently default to the declared-boolean FALSE pattern because entry preparation cannot yet populate those lists" — so the component is effectively zero everywhere post-fix, while the Brazil atoms cite 9903.05.01 "articles the product of Brazil" with named exclusions. A reviewer may want to treat this half as a separate, opposite-direction item (possible fail-closed regression) rather than part of the same finding; the PR excuses it as outside the April-June evaluation window.
3. The brand-new `section_232_steel_component_rate` + `ch03_s232_steel_heading_rate` and the new `+ section_232_steel_component_rate` stack term. The PR frames this as coverage "the witness never had" and the module previously claimed only the witness's component set, so per the task rule this is added coverage, not a defect.

Provenance caveats for the reviewer (not part of the verdict): the new steel rule is emitted with a double-nested `metadata: proof: proof: atoms:`, which the PR's own issue comment confirms was repaired later ("steel atoms unwrapped to canonical `metadata.proof.atoms`"); the PR body says the steel rate is "grounded on the consolidated HTS 9903.82.02 provision" while the atoms cite 9903.81.87/.88; and under the pinned corpus (us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap, Rev 3 notes) `us/statute/hts/9903.81.87` does not resolve at all and `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-221` returns IEEPA reciprocal notes containing neither "9903.03.03" nor "surcharge", so the §122 exception excerpts could not be verified against source at their cited paths (those atoms are unchanged by this commit, so the mismatch predates it).
